description: Traces and metrics of the requisition system, exported by the API and the worker to the local observability stack.

panels.description: Requests per second, measured at the HTTP server. Every route the API serves counts once, including the ones that failed.
panels.title: Requests

panels.description: How long the API takes to answer, from the histogram otelgin records. p99 is the one that reacts to a slow dependency first.
panels.title: Request latency

panels.description: Share of requests the API answered with a 5xx. Auth failures and bad requests are 4xx and deliberately not counted here.
panels.title: 5xx error ratio

panels.description: Which endpoints are being hit, and how often.
panels.title: Requests by route

panels.description: Invitations an admin created, split by whether the use case reported success or an error. A failed attempt means an invitation was not sent.
panels.title: Invitations — outcome

panels.description: How long the invitation use case takes end to end, including the email handoff. This is the business operation, not the HTTP request.
panels.title: Invitations — duration

panels.description: Acceptance attempts by the invitee, split by outcome. A failure here means a valid invitation was not accepted.
panels.title: Acceptances — outcome

panels.description: How long the acceptance use case takes end to end.
panels.title: Acceptances — duration

panels.description: Invitation emails the worker delivered, split by outcome. A failure is an email the worker could not send, and it is retried by asynq.
panels.title: Email delivery — outcome

panels.description: How long delivering one invitation email takes, measured in the worker, not in the HTTP request that queued it.
panels.title: Email delivery — duration

panels.description: Expired invitations the worker swept, split by outcome.
panels.title: Invitation expirations — outcome

panels.description: How long the expiry sweep takes per batch.
panels.title: Invitation expirations — duration

panels.description: How long a Postgres query takes, from the histogram otelsql records. It is a metric rather than a trace query, so it holds even when the traces of the moment were not sampled.
panels.title: Postgres — query duration

panels.description: p95 and p99 of every Redis span, computed from the traces with TraceQL.
panels.title: Redis — command duration

panels.description: Connections held by each process's Redis pool, by state. Redis commands are not timed by the client, so this is what the pool publishes.
panels.title: Redis — connections

panels.description: Traces matching the selected services, newest first. Open one to see the whole request, from the HTTP handler down through Postgres and Redis.
panels.title: Traces

title: Requisition System
